item.title: Hug a user is here! Tell us what’s broken, we’ll fix it
item.description:
We’re starting something new at daily.dev called Hug a User.


The idea is simple: Every week, each engineer gets up to half a day to fix a bug or ship a small feature that came directly from you. No tickets. No sprints. No begging for approvals (unless it’s the homepage, then yes, still sacred ground).



Basically, it’s your chance to have an engineer swoop in, cape and all, and make that one annoying thing disappear.


What counts?



  • Fixing a bug that’s been haunting you

  • Polishing rough edges that slow you down

  • Small features that would make your daily.dev experience smoother


What doesn’t count?



  • Asking us to build GitHub 2.0 in half a day

  • Secret plots to sneak your pet feature onto the homepage


So, tell us what’s the one bug, frustration, or small improvement you’d love to see us tackle in Hug a User?


Drop it in the comments, and who knows, next week you might log in and it’ll just be fixed.


(And yes, if you’ve ever cursed at daily.dev under your breath, now’s the time to turn that energy into a feature request.)

item.title: Talking to an LLM
item.description:
My biggest cheat for 10x-ing the quality I get from ChatGPT? I talk to it. Literally.


There’s a simple rule in knowledge work: You can think more than you can say, and you can say more than you can type.


When it comes to working with LLMs, this matters a lot. Because the biggest unlock isn’t in the model… it’s in the context you give it.


Typing long, nuanced prompts is tedious. Most people start optimizing for brevity instead of clarity. But the thing is that LLMs thrive on context. The more details you give, the better the outcome.


That’s why I stopped typing, and started talking. Whether it’s ChatGPT, Claude, or Grok, I just speak my thoughts out loud. It feels weird at first (like talking to yourself), but it’s a real force multiplier.


If the tool you’re using has built-in voice transcription (like ChatGPT does), use it. If not, pair it with something like SuperWhisper. It works like magic.


This one shift has helped me 10x the quality of my work across product, marketing, operations, and sales. It’s my unfair advantage and I hereby offer it to you all for free :)


Highly recommend giving it a try.

item.title: What makes you actually reply to a recruiter?
item.description:
Most recruiter DMs on LinkedIn are noise… generic messages, AI slop, missing details, or roles that don’t fit at all.


But imagine one shows up that actually catches your eye.
What’s the very first thing you look for before you even think about replying?


Is it comp, tech stack, company name, remote policy, growth path… or something else entirely?


I’m not asking for the full wishlist… just the one or two signals that make you pause and think, “ok, maybe this is worth a look.”


Curious to hear what matters most to you
